title: Fancy Zones just mixed up the monitors

judgment.rationale: The latest report confirms repeatable layout swaps after sleep on two monitors with different orientations and custom layouts. The monitor identity/reconciliation path is a plausible area, but no current runtime capture proves where the identity changes.
evidence: The latest comment says the issue is consistent on two monitors, one horizontal and one vertical, each with a custom layout.
After sleep/resume the layouts swap, and reopening the editor and reassigning them is the current workaround.

proposed_fixes.title: Reconcile per-monitor layouts after display wake
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: after sleep/wake re-enumerates the mixed-orientation displays, FancyZones associates saved work-area layouts with a changed monitor identity/order and restores them to the opposite display.
plan: Compare stable monitor device identities and FancyZones work-area IDs before sleep and after wake.
If identity/order changes, reconcile saved layouts using stable display identity rather than transient enumeration order.
Add a regression for two differently oriented monitors with distinct custom layouts across sleep/resume.
verification: After repeated sleep/resume cycles, each monitor retains its own assigned layout.
Changing display enumeration order does not swap layout assignments.

reproduce.title: Reconcile per-monitor layouts after display wake
prerequisites: FancyZones enabled with distinct custom layouts assigned to each display.
setup: Assign one custom layout to the horizontal display and a different custom layout to the vertical display.
steps: Confirm each display shows its intended layout.
Put the computer to sleep and resume it.
Reopen the FancyZones editor and check whether the layouts remain associated with the same physical displays.
Repeat once with display enumeration/order noted before and after resume.
reproduce.expected_result: Each physical monitor retains its own custom layout after wake.

comment.body: Thanks for confirming the mixed-orientation, two-monitor reproduction on 0.102.3101. Could you share a screenshot of the FancyZones layout assignment on each physical display immediately before sleep and after resume, and note whether Windows changes the display arrangement? This will help distinguish a layout restore error from a changed monitor/work-area mapping.
